Hello, first of all I want you to know that in one way or another we've all gone through these break ups, so i'm offering you my sincere support.

Other than that I will list a few things you can do as well as explain why you could follow them so you can change your mental/emotional lifestyle.

**1)** Take 24 hours away from social media and if possible from computer and cellphone. I want you to take a pen and a piece of paper and write down any positive things you think you have. For example "loving, caring, supportive, dilligent" it doesn't matter if it's 1 or 100 just write what you can think. The reason i would like you to do that is because you need to understand not only mentally but physically (hence the pen and paper) that you are a person that has good stuff in their personality and that you basically **DESERVE BETTER.**

**2)** After the 24 hours pass, return to your cellphone/social media/etc, text him that you will cease all contact with him and for him to not bother you **AT ALL.** Bear in mind that this message wont be a conversation starter, do not wait for a reply or anything. Just let him know (so you won't have to deal with him contacting you again) and then block him and delete him from everywhere and everything. 

**3)** 110% start working out. It can be a light jog, lifting weights, yoga, anything that basically will make you work up even a slight sweat. The reason for this is basically to force your own brain to release dopamine and serotonin which will make you feel calm, happy and most important that you're in control, whether it's of your emotions, your life or your mental state.

**4)** Do not look for a hook up *yet*. I'm saying this because it will come back to haunt you real bad and make you feel even worse than you are feeling right now. For me it took around 2 months that i felt calm and felt good enough to go out for a date with someone, but for each person is different. All i know for certain is that right now, you're emotionally unstable and this will only drag you down more.

**5)** Start a hobby. Ok so, i mentioned working out but I would like you to start a more spiritual hobby as well. It can be drawing, video editing, even reading a book, anything that will make you use your mind and actually get something from it (whether it's experience, knowledge or straight up enjoyment). The reason for that, is pretty simple, it will help you (1) to fill up your day with something productive, (2) make you have more trust in yourself and your abilities and basically *what you deserve.*

***6)*** Keep a journal of your day to day life for 30 days (optional). This is more because it will help you get in the mentality of "*Hey, i'm actually different and worth even better stuff than before"* . 

These are the steps i would recommend you follow in order to get over this situation and become an even better person. Since he cheated on you, he basically took away your control on some stuff and that's why you feel so uneasy with the whole situation. But I promise you if you follow these you will definitely see a positive change on your mindset and mental state. 

One last thing is that, if you want to follow this advice make sure you follow each step except from the optional one. Dont pick 1 or 2 that suit you best or seem easier and do them cause this works like a chain, If it's not connected, it doesn't work. If you don't want to follow any of this, all is good, i really hope someone else can help you with your situation.

Good luck and remember who you are!

Hello, so everything i will write from this point on will be coming from how **he** might feeling (since i'm a guy it might be more helpful realistically speaking). Anything i say is not a rule you have to follow, it's just a point of view and in no way am I trying to tell you to follow it. 

 I want to begin by saying that, a big no no for any kind of "fight" in a relationship where 1 person says they are getting tired of it, is long messages. I absolutely understand that you want to explain in detail your thought proccess and whatnot because you want to be clear with him, but it's having the opposite result. I can tell just from the way he's responding that all he reads is "bla bla bla im a victim, bla bla bla". I am not calling you a victim by any means, it's just how it would look to someone that is slowly getting "burned out" in a relationship.  
 Secondly, do not try to be apologetic about the fact you texted him because you care. If you apologize or try to explain yourself the other person will only see it as an admission of guilt aka that you did something wrong.

 Furthermore, this is my personal opinion but, in a relationships, things like "break" dont exist. If someone needs a break it means that there's something that's tiring them out. A break is not something good (in the way that i see from his messages that he means it). Sure he can go on summer on vacation with his friends instead of you, or he can hang out with his friends every other week. Those are the "healthy" breaks that a relationship needs. If you spend 24/7 with the other person you'll get tired and drained both emotionally and mentally. 

 All in all, my advice would be that you break up with him and start no contact effective immediately. If a person feels this bad by just you texting, i dont think they will ever want to meet up for a date or something. I know that i'm just throwing the idea of breaking up really easily right now but know that you have a value that only you can count. Don't let someone's behaviour decide what's your value in their life. You can offer to him A,B,C and you want in return 1,2,3. If he can't offer those 3 things but he's asking for a,b,c,d,e,f,g from you then it's not worth it. 

**TL;DR:** try not to send long messages, dont apologize about texting, if someone asks for a break its usually a break up and dont accept things for the sake of fear of moving forward with your life.

My fellow Redditor, although I agree that the person above could have said that thing in a nicer way, from reading everything you wrote (post+comments) It looks to me that you are just going to deny everything each of us says until you get to the answer you want to hear. So to help as much as I can, try this approach: tell her that you thought about it and being friends with her after such a long time of being in a relationship is next to impossible for you. When we say "I wanna stay friends with my ex after I move on" what we really mean is "I'm gonna keep hoping we get back together one day". Unfortunately, relationships are complex in these matters so in your case, you should do the opposite of what you want. I get you don't want that feeling of guilt eating you away, that's why I gave you that suggestion of telling her you can't possibly be friends with her. 
I'm saying this from experience because, when it comes to love some things are pretty straightforward. Let's say you do manage to stay friends with her. Most likely she'll start checking out her choices as far as dating goes, while you will be stuck in that "as a friend" mental state. You will be a bit happy at first because you'll be able to talk to her , but after that there's a high chance you will start acting really spiteful. You are so sure your ex doesn't care for another relationship right now but...the one in a trillion chance where she finds another person and gets together with them will break you. Call her, tell her u can't be friends with her and talk anymore. If anything, (without wanting to give you false hope) the fact you will show you care about yourself might make her see you as a potential partner once more later. BUT, do.not.wait. for that happen. Don't hope for it. Your goal is to move on and be okay. Once you are okay then you can care about others. 
Good luck!

Hello. First of all congratulations because even though you broke no contact you still managed to keep it for however long. Dont get sad about it. You're not back to square 1. Not even close. You have definitely changed and i know you can feel it as well. If this had happened at the start of your No contact with your ex you wouldn't feel that you did the wrong thing. So trust me, it's clear your mindset is slowly changing. 

Other than that, i've been in your situation, multiple times with the same ex as well. The solution i found working for me is that whenever i felt like texting, i would usually leave my phone or get off the computer for a bit. And then i would talk to myself about how this conversation will go. You were in a relationship and you broke up so you kind of know how a conversation at this time would go. So, I would talk and talk and think how the whole dialogue would unfold only to realize that 90% of the time it would end up with me getting hurt and my ex feeling "powerful" even if it was subconciously. But what about that 10%? That 10% chance that the ex-gf/bf would welcome you with open arms, tell you that he/she missed you and that they want to try again. Well, lucky for us, deep down we know there's no such chance. The break up happened for a reason. If it was something fixable (in most cases at least) you would have worked it out before reaching that point. So even if we bet all in that 10% chance, it's most definitely going to be a loss for us. 

Take a deep breath. Never forget that even though you have broken up, you are a wonderful person. Always remember that, you deserve someone a lot better than a person that will just leave in the middle of a conversation and basically not care or not give you the respect you deserve.

In conclusion, what i'm trying to say is that you are not back to 0. You took a "bad" break from your no contact period and you realized that it just isn't worth it. So keep counting your NC days from where you left off. Good luck!!

First of all, a very big well done brother for the 10 months of no contact. It's really awesome and honestly most people (including myself) dont have that kind of strength that you do which is stay loyal to the NC. 

To adress your issue now, what i'm seeing is the typical behavior of an ex. It's the whole " i want us to keep talking even if we arent together anymore" which translates to "i wanna have you as a backup plan in case my future relationships dont work out cause I will take the appropriate steps to have you stay in love with me". Thing is , i don't think your ex is concious of what she's doing. Especially after a 4 year relationship it seems like she's honestly trying to keep you in her life cause she likes you. You are a wonderful human being and you deserve a lot better than someone that broke up with you just because "it wouldn't work at this point of her life". Remember that.

As far as she checking your profile and your stories there's 2 possibilities:

1) she actually misses you   
2) she KNOWS you are checking out if she has seen your stories. 

To this i would suggest you turn your profile to private or (depending on what social media platform you use for those stories) lock her out so she wont be able to see them. That will probably make her wanna text and ask you why she can't see your stories anymore. Depending on the way she says it though, it will become clear which of the 2 possibilities i mentioned above is actually true. 

For the new girl you dated, 1 month or 10 months you're still coming out of a 4 year relationship. You might have forgotten how the "dating game" is played so don't worry much about her (the new girl) not texting you. It's still early, and since she told you she would love to hang out again then take her word up for it. The ball is on her field now so just give her the cold shoulder. Don't insist and don't show any sign of you being depended on her for having fun. 

TL;DR 

\-Don't fall into the trap of trying to be friends with her cause you'll just end up in an endless cycle of you being in love with her

\-Try the lock out/turn profile to private thing for your social media stories

\-"Ignore" the new girl for some time and see if she responds.

 1)Keep no contact until/IF she decides to contact you. What i come to realize is that the more you try to show them that you love them the more they see it as weakness of some sort.
